marks.gloss_en: אי מה חגיגה בעלי חיים, אף סוכה נמי בעלי חיים! -- if so, as the chagiga is of animals, the sukkah too should be of animals
כי אתא רבין אמר רבי יוחנן, אמר קרא: באספך מגרנך ומיקבך -- the source given for the sekhakh principle (for R' Akiva, per the stam's question at 11b.15)
R' Yochanan per Ravin: the sekhakh law derives from 'when you gather in from your threshing floor and from your winepress' (Devarim 16:13)
רב חסדא אמר מהכא: צאו ההר והביאו ... -- the source given for the sekhakh principle
Rav Chisda: the sekhakh law derives from 'go out to the mountain and bring olive leaves, and oil-tree leaves, and myrtle leaves, and palm leaves, and leaves of a thick tree' (Nechemya 8:15)
ואימא גורן עצמו ויקב עצמו! -- say the verse means the threshing floor itself and the winepress itself (Steinsaltz: the produce, which is susceptible to impurity)
יקב כתיב כאן, ואי אפשר לסכך בו -- attacked by R' Yirmeya and conceded at 12a.4 (carried by p_zeira_yekev; header)
R' Zeira: 'winepress' is written, and one cannot roof with it -- so the verse cannot mean the winepress itself
מגרנך ולא גורן עצמו, מיקבך ולא יקב עצמו (= p_ashi_velo_goren_atzmo)
Rav Ashi: 'FROM your threshing floor' -- not the threshing floor itself; 'FROM your winepress' -- not the winepress itself
מתקיף לה רבי ירמיה: ואימא יין קרוש הבא משניר שהוא דומה לעיגולי דבילה! -- say congealed wine from Senir, which is like cakes of pressed figs (and could be roofed with)
Rav Chisda: the verse's 'myrtle' is wild myrtle, for the sukkah
R' Yochanan's own account of the bundles (lest he roof with what he set out to dry) shows the bundles ruling is the storehouse decree
by elimination from R' Yaakov's report of two reasons: if the bundles are the decree, the hollowed stack is תעשה ולא מן העשוי

R' Yochanan: why may one not roof with bundles? at times a man comes from the field with his bundle on his shoulder and lays it on his sukkah to dry it, and then decides to use it as roofing -- and the Torah said 'you shall make', not from what is already made
אטו חבילי קש ... משום תעשה ולא מן העשוי ליכא? והחוטט בגדיש משום גזרת אוצר ליכא? -- both reasons seem to apply to both cases
ורבי יוחנן אמר לך: 'אין מסככין' is lechatchila, for the decree, and Torah law allows it; 'אינה סוכה' is even bediavad, from the Torah (= p_chavilot_lechatchila, p_chotet_deoraita)
where the mishnah says 'one may not roof with them', it is ab initio, for the storehouse decree; by Torah law it is fine
bundles of straw, wood and twigs: one may not roof a sukkah with them
one who hollows out a grain-stack to make himself a sukkah: it is not a sukkah
R' Yochanan: of the two halakhot (bundles; the hollowed stack) one is due to the storehouse decree and one to 'you shall make' and not from what is already made -- the two rest on DIFFERENT reasons
